# Valkey.app

> Valkey.app is a free, open-source (Apache 2.0), native macOS app for running Valkey — the open-source,
> BSD-licensed Redis alternative maintained under the Linux Foundation — on a Mac. It is to Valkey what
> Postgres.app is to PostgreSQL: local servers without Homebrew, Docker or a terminal.

- Runs on macOS 13 Ventura or later, Apple Silicon and Intel (universal binaries).
- Several Valkey servers side by side, each with its own name, port, Valkey version, data directory and live log.
- Valkey versions (7.2, 8.0, 8.1, 9.0, 9.1 and 9.2 lines) and official modules (JSON, Bloom, Search) install from a signed
  registry, so new releases arrive without an app update. Every download is verified against an Ed25519-signed
  list of SHA-256 checksums.
- Modules are added per server and matched to the server's Valkey version.
- Search module (vector and full-text, FT.*): Valkey 9.1 and 9.2 only; on macOS its index memory isn't counted in
  Valkey's used_memory or maxmemory.
- Menu-bar icon to start, stop and connect with valkey-cli; the app updates itself (with confirmation).
- `valkey-app` command line with `--json` output: everything the UI does, scriptable by people and AI agents.
- Not yet notarized by Apple (a free side project; Apple's paid developer account is planned). On first launch,
  allow it once in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway (macOS 15+) or Control-click → Open
  (macOS 13–14).

## Verify a download

- Source is public (Apache 2.0); release DMGs are built by GitHub Actions from the tagged commit
  (.github/workflows/release-app.yml).
- Every release's notes list SHA-256 checksums of Valkey.dmg and Valkey.app.zip.
- Releases after 1.5 carry a GitHub build-provenance attestation:
  `gh attestation verify Valkey.dmg -R alhassanaraouf/Valkey.app`
- Newer release notes link a VirusTotal scan of Valkey.dmg.
- App updates are Ed25519-signed; Valkey and module downloads are checked against the Ed25519-signed registry.json.

## Install

- Download Valkey.dmg, open it, drag Valkey.app into Applications.
- Or with Homebrew (installs the app, not the `valkey` server formula):

  brew install --cask alhassanaraouf/tap/valkey
